liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Morning Dew** (7 reviews): Garcia repeats the 'guess it doesn't matter' line, growing more passionate each time, then resolves it powerfully; Garcia nearly forgot the song's musical arrangement; a St. Stephen tease comes right before it [10][11][13][14][17][18][19]
- **Scarlet Begonias** (2 reviews): Reviewer finds the Scarlet unmemorable, with little jamming as it moves into Fire; Reviewer disagrees that the Scarlet is weak and loves the Scarlet into Fire [14][15]
- **I Know You Rider** (1 review): China Cat into Rider sits in an unusual spot in the set but is played well [11]

## Setlist highlights

- **Morning Dew**: back after 119 archived shows (572 days) [22]

## The recordings

- **gd79-11-08.sbd.litfin.18126.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 20 songs; 150 min; rated 4.31/5 by 26 [1]. Said about its sound: Reviewer calls the recording's sound quality superb; Phil's bass is crisp and powerful in the recording; Sound quality is high, with Lesh very loud and prominent throughout Morning Dew [12][13][14][15][17][18][19]
- **gd1979-11-08.169456.aud.composite.wagner.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 20 songs; 144 min [2]
- **gd1979-11-08.set2.sbd.lai.3901.shnf**: soundboard; 16 songs; 109 min; rated 2.5/5 by 2 [6]
- **gd1979-11-08.set2-sbd.lai.macneil.8546.shnf**: soundboard; 11 songs; 78 min; rated 4.5/5 by 4 [7]

## Around the show

- Mickey strikes an anvil as a sound effect [11]
- The crowd sounds very excited, including during the Scarlet into Fire [17]
- A dew was also found out in the parking lot after the show, a pun on the song [20]
- The set closes with Not Fade Away into Dew, Johnny B. Goode, and a four-second track of Bobby saying goodnight [6]
- The correct ending is Not Fade Away into Dew, Johnny B. Goode, then Bobby saying 'thank you, goodnight' [7]
- Reviewer says this is the only Morning Dew of 1979 and one of their favorite Phil Dews [13]
- Morning Dew was rarely played in this era, and this one is a good one [15]
- Dew had been absent 19 months since 4/15/78, and this was the only one of 1979 [18]
- Reviewer says this Dew does not rank among the best-ever versions [19]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd79-11-08.sbd.litfin.18126.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [1]. Also: Source chain listed as SBD>MR>D>CDR; one set text file gives a revised chain SBD>Cm>Cass>Dat>CD; This shn merges the earlier separate set 1 and set 2 seeds; seeded to etree by D Litfin, who edited and encoded [1]
- **gd1979-11-08.169456.aud.composite.wagner.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Bob Wagner; transferred by Scott Clugston, Charlie Miller; source: Source A: Unknown audience cassettes > ? > Bob Wagner's cassettes (believed to be 1st generation) supplies "New Minglewood Blues", the first half of "Stagger… [2]. Also: An unknown audience source patches 1:36 of Drums; another patches the last 2:37 of Stagger Lee plus short snippets elsewhere [2]
- **gd1979-11-08.set2.sbd.lai.3901.shnf**: transferred by Mike Lai; source: SBD> Cm> Cass> Dat> Sound Forge> CD (including digital noise reduction) [6]. Also: This seed contains only set 2, though the md5s suggest more; some tracks repeat Lost Sailor through Space [6]
- **gd1979-11-08.set2-sbd.lai.macneil.8546.shnf**: transferred by Mike Lai; source: SBD> Cm> Cass> Dat> Sound Forge> CD (including digital noise reduction) [7]. Also: This set 2 seed cuts in partway through a lyric; its track names mislead, repeating Lost Sailor through Space [7]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead Capital Centre - November 8, 1979](https://www.dead.net/show/november-8-1979) [23]
- Poster by Jerry Garcia: [1979-11-08 Backstage Pass - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/image/1979-11-08-backstage-pass/) [24]
